business_definition: Share of sellable unit-nights that were actually occupied. The operational basis: units that cannot be sold are not counted as missed sales.
caveats: Differs from occupancy_pct_benchmark by the share of inventory out of order. Report the basis alongside the number or the two figures will be read as an error.

business_definition: Occupancy against full physical inventory, the basis used for STR-style external comparison.
caveats: Always lower than the operational basis. Deliberately published alongside it so the gap is visible rather than surprising.

business_definition: Average Daily Rate: net room revenue per occupied unit-night, excluding tax.
caveats: Includes hourly microstays, which bill at roughly 28% of a nightly rate and pull ADR down. adr_excl_microstay_inr is published alongside for that reason.

business_definition: ADR over nightly stays only, excluding hourly microstay inventory.
caveats: The honest comparison figure when benchmarking against nightly-only operators.

business_definition: Revenue per Available Room-night: the single number that reflects both rate and volume.
formula_text: Net Room Revenue / Rooms Available  ==  ADR x Occupancy
caveats: RevPAR = ADR x Occupancy holds exactly ONLY because all three read the same table and the same denominator. Asserted in tests. RevPAR is also indifferent between 100% at INR 3,000 and 60% at INR 5,000, which have very different cost per occupied unit -- do not optimise it alone.

business_definition: Room revenue net of GST and net of discount, before OTA commission.
caveats: Recognised on STAY DATE, not booking or payment date. Marketing reporting on booking date and Finance on payment date will legitimately produce different totals for the same month.

business_definition: What the guest actually paid, including GST at the rate applicable to that stay date and nightly rate.
caveats: Spans the 22 Sep 2025 GST change (12% slab abolished; 5% no-ITC at or below INR 7,500, 18% with ITC above). An apparent step in gross revenue across that date is a TAX artefact, not performance -- which is why the net measure is the one used for rate metrics.

business_definition: Share of bookings made in the period that were subsequently cancelled.
caveats: Deliberately measured on cohort basis -- cancellations OF bookings made in the period -- not cancellations occurring in the period. The two give materially different numbers and answer different questions: cohort basis measures booking quality, event basis measures this period's revenue loss. State which one you mean.

business_definition: Share of room-nights sold through each distribution channel.
formula_text: Room-nights per channel / Total room-nights x 100
caveats: Measured on room-nights, not booking count: corporate books longer stays, so a booking-count mix overstates OTA share.

business_definition: Mean days between booking and arrival. Short lead times leave less room to reprice.
caveats: Indian booking windows run 7-21 days against a ~40-day global average, so pickup analysis here should use 0/1/3/7/14-day windows rather than the textbook 30/60/90.
Uses the half-open interval: departure night is not a night. Counting it inflates ALOS by 1 and room-nights by roughly 1/ALOS.

business_definition: Wall-clock minutes from a guest raising a request to its resolution.
caveats: WALL-CLOCK, not business hours. These are 24-hour serviced apartments and a guest waiting at 02:00 is still waiting. A business-hours clock would report this as excellent.

business_definition: Share of resolved requests that exceeded the target resolution time for their request type.
caveats: The blended rate hides property- and daypart-level failure. A 0.9pp portfolio move concealed a 2.6x degradation at one property in one shift. Always segment before concluding.

business_definition: Mean guest satisfaction score on resolved service requests, 1-5.
caveats: Response rate is roughly a third, so CSAT carries selection bias: guests who respond are not a random sample. Report the response rate next to the score.

business_definition: Share of guests with two or more completed stays, after deterministic identity resolution.
formula_text: Guests with >=2 stays / Total guests x 100
caveats: Published on the RESOLVED basis. The raw basis understates loyalty because duplicate profiles split one guest into several; mart.v_guest_repeat exposes both so the size of that understatement is visible.

business_definition: Directly attributable acquisition and processing cost per confirmed booking: OTA commission plus payment gateway fees and the GST charged on both.
formula_text: (Commission + Gateway Fee + GST on fees) / Confirmed Bookings
caveats: This is a DIRECT cost per booking, not a fully loaded cost, and must not be presented as one. GOPPAR is uncomputable on this dataset for the same reason: no departmental cost data. Saying so is more useful than publishing a fully-loaded-looking number built on invented overhead.
